issues.legal_issue: A conviction in a case based on circumstantial evidence may be sustained only when the proved circumstances form a complete chain that excludes every reasonable hypothesis consistent with innocence.
material_facts: There were no eyewitnesses to the assault, and the prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence.
The accused and deceased were related, and a dispute over partition of family land provided a possible motive.
The deceased’s gold ornaments, a weapon, and bloodstained clothing were recovered from the accused or at his instance on the day after the body was found.
Forensic examination established that the seized clothing bore bloodstains, and the accused gave no explanation for possession of the deceased’s articles.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances, considered cumulatively, were sufficient to sustain the conviction, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The prosecution must prove each incriminating circumstance beyond reasonable doubt, and the circumstances must be conclusive, consistent only with guilt, and form a complete chain excluding reasonable hypotheses of innocence. A false or absent defence cannot cure gaps in the prosecution case. The Court relied on Hukam Singh v. State of Rajasthan, Eradu v. State of Hyderabad, Earabhadrappa v. State of Karnataka, State of U.P. v. Sukhbasi, Balwinder Singh v. State of Punjab, Ashok Kumar Chatterjee v. State of M.P., Bhagat Ram v. State of Punjab, C. Chenga Reddy v. State of A.P., Padala Veera Reddy v. State of A.P., State of U.P. v. Ashok Kumar Srivastava, Hanumant Govind Nargundkar v. State of M.P., and Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra.

predicates.appeal_against_circumstantial_evidence_c: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a conviction based on circumstantial evidence.
predicates.incriminating_circumstances_proved_beyon: The prosecution proved the incriminating circumstances beyond reasonable doubt.
predicates.circumstances_form_complete_chain: The proved circumstances were connected and together formed a complete evidentiary chain.
predicates.chain_excludes_reasonable_innocent_hypot: The complete chain was inconsistent with reasonable explanations other than the accused’s guilt.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conviction based on circumstantial evidence, the conviction is sustained if the prosecution proves the incriminating circumstances beyond reasonable doubt and those circumstances form a complete chain excluding reasonable innocent hypotheses.

issues.legal_issue: Information given by an accused in police custody is admissible only to the extent that it relates distinctly to a fact discovered because of that information.
material_facts: The accused appeared before the investigating officer and was taken into custody.
Following information given by the accused, the deceased’s gold articles, a weapon, and the accused’s bloodstained clothing were recovered from places associated with the accused.
Witness testimony supported the recoveries, and forensic examination confirmed bloodstains on the seized clothing.
issues.conclusion: The discovery-related information and resulting recoveries were admissible to the extent they related distinctly to the facts discovered.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 25 and 26 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 generally bar proof of confessions made to police or while in police custody; Section 27 permits proof of only so much information as relates distinctly to a fact discovered in consequence of it. The discovered fact includes the place from which an object is produced and the accused’s knowledge of that place, not merely the object itself. The Court relied on Pulukuri Kottaya v. Emperor, State of Uttar Pradesh v. Deoman Upadhyaya, Mohmed Inayatullah v. State of Maharashtra, Earabhadrappa alias Krishnappa v. State of Karnataka, and State of Maharashtra v. Damu.

predicates.criminal_case_relying_on_accused_led_dis: The criminal proceeding relies on a discovery made after information from the accused.
predicates.accused_in_police_custody: The accused gave the information while in police custody.
predicates.information_caused_discovery: The information led investigators to discover a fact or object not previously located by them.
predicates.information_distinctly_related_to_discov: The information directly identified the discovered fact, including the relevant place or the accused’s knowledge of it.

issues.definition: In a criminal case relying on an accused-led discovery, information given in police custody is admissible to the extent it caused and directly relates to the discovered fact.

issues.legal_issue: Recent, unexplained possession of a deceased person’s property may support an inference of guilt when the circumstances connect the possession and the killing and corroborate that inference.
material_facts: The deceased’s gold chain and ring were recovered at the accused’s instance on the day after the body was found.
The accused did not explain the lawful origin of his possession of the deceased’s articles.
A weapon and the accused’s bloodstained clothing were also recovered, and forensic examination confirmed bloodstains on the clothing.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the recent, unexplained possession of the deceased’s articles, considered with the other circumstances, supported an inference that the accused committed the murder.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 114, Illustration (a), of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, a court may draw an inference from recent possession of stolen property, with the timing and circumstances assessed in each case; possession alone does not automatically prove murder. Section 106 may also be relevant to facts especially within the accused’s knowledge, but it does not displace the prosecution’s burden. The Court relied on J.P. Anand v. D.G. Baffna, Ezhil v. State of Tamil Nadu, Gulab Chand v. State of M.P., Sanwat Khan v. State of Rajasthan, Tulsiram Kanu v. State, Earabhadrappa v. State of Karnataka, Mukund alias Kundu Mishra v. State of M.P., and Ronny alias Ronald James Alwaris v. State of Maharashtra.

predicates.murder_conviction_case: The proceeding concerns whether the accused is guilty of murder.
predicates.deceased_property_found_in_accused_posse: Property belonging to the deceased was found in the accused’s possession soon after the death.
predicates.accused_gave_no_lawful_explanation: The accused did not provide a plausible lawful explanation for possessing the deceased’s property.
predicates.other_circumstances_connect_possession_t: Other proved circumstances connected the possession with the killing, rather than leaving possession as the only evidence.

issues.definition: In a murder case, recent possession of the deceased’s property without a lawful explanation supports an inference of murder guilt when other proved circumstances connect that possession to the killing.
